title: Add up 1 to n
prompt:
Byte wants to know 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n. Write a loop that adds each number into `total`. Use the accumulator pattern: `total` starts at 0 and grows by one number on every pass.

When it works, `python3 total.py` prints `Sum: 55`. The tests also try `n = 1` and `n = 100`. Watch the end of your `range()`.
hints: `for k in range(...):` hands you one number at a time. Inside the loop, add `k` to `total`.
`range(1, n)` stops one short of `n`. You need the end to be one past the last number you want.
`for k in range(1, n + 1):` and, indented under it, `total = total + k`.
explain_after: `range()` never includes its end point [py-064], so `range(1, n + 1)` gives 1 up to and including `n`. Forgetting the `+ 1` is the classic off-by-one error: the program runs, prints a number and is quietly wrong.
